svg.title: The fly connectome's head-direction ring inside the whole simulated resting brain: a bump of activity in the ellipsoid body holds a heading with no cue and wanders slowly, visiting every heading once each ring neuron's excitability has adapted in place
svg.text: The connectome's compass, inside the whole resting brain
its EPGs' bump holds a heading with no cue and wanders slowly, like a fly's in darkness
16 wedges, lit by their EPGs' spikes; 40 s at 5× real time
The same run over 120 s: where the bump sits
This run drifts at D = 0.008 rad²/s; flies' bumps in darkness, about 0.003–0.04.
